title: arXiv physics notable papers — announcement batch 12 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred editorial shortlist, not a popularity ranking; citation and independent-attention evidence is sparse for recent papers. Semantic Scholar citation metadata was unavailable, so no citation-momentum claims are made.

sections.title: Observation of a Threshold Enhancement in the π⁰π⁰ Mass Spectrum in ψ(3686) → π⁰π⁰J/ψ Decays
sections.published: Not available from the sources checked; submitted 2026-10-09
sections.abstract: BESIII reports a greater-than-10σ neutral-pion-channel confirmation of a near-threshold enhancement in ψ(3686) decays, with a fitted mass of 274.3 MeV/c² and width of 17.1 MeV.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find a neutral-channel threshold enhancement consistent in mass and width with the charged-pion-channel feature; their QCD multipole-expansion model describes the full spectrum better than the tested chiral-perturbation model.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; BESIII ψ(3686) data and fits including final-state interactions.
sections.unique_caveat: The fit significance establishes a spectral feature, not its underlying state or mechanism; the abstract reports model-dependent descriptions rather than a unique interpretation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A large BESIII sample of 2.712 billion ψ(3686) events and a reported >10σ confirmation make this the clearest direct experimental result in the batch; scientific-evidence signal, not popularity.

sections.title: Lattice Monte Carlo of λϕ⁴ on Euclidean de Sitter
sections.abstract: The paper introduces a spherical-harmonic spectral-lattice Monte Carlo simulation of massless λϕ⁴ theory on Euclidean de Sitter space and reports weak-coupling agreement with stochastic equilibrium plus strong-coupling saturation.
sections.claimed_result: The author reports nonperturbative support for stochastic resummation of light-scalar infrared effects in de Sitter and finds the renormalized quartic coupling saturates near the one-loop RG-flow ceiling at strong bare coupling.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; spectral lattice on S⁴, with Monte Carlo time series and code advertised by the author.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract describes a massless λϕ⁴ setup and finite-cutoff method; the result does not by itself establish behavior for other fields or quantum-gravity theories.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A claimed first Monte Carlo treatment of quantum field theory on Euclidean de Sitter, cross-listed across theory, gravity and lattice physics, with data and code linked from the record.

sections.title: A Single Line-Emitter Identified in an Unbiased Search with JWST/NIRSpec: Multi-Object Coronagraphy for Slitless Spectroscopy
sections.abstract: Using a new JWST/NIRSpec slitless-search configuration, the authors report a repeat-detected 1.60 μm emission line in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field with no known imaging counterpart and discuss possible AGN or transient origins.
sections.claimed_result: The measured line flux is (2.5 ± 0.3) × 10⁻¹⁸ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² with FWHM 13.2 ± 2.0 Å; the inferred lower bound on observed-frame equivalent width is 7620 Å, making several common line identifications difficult.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; JWST/NIRSpec G140M/F100LP spectroscopy in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field.
sections.unique_caveat: It is a single-line object with no identified redshift or source class; AGN and transient explanations remain possibilities, not conclusions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors report detection in four dither positions and two position angles, and the arXiv record says the paper is published in ApJ; observational repeatability and publication signal, not popularity.

sections.title: Enhanced Coulomb pseudopotentials in high-pressure hydrides from first principles
sections.abstract: First-principles calculations find substantially larger Coulomb pseudopotentials than the commonly assumed range in several superconducting hydrides, with a reported 40 K reduction in the estimated critical temperature for Mg₂IrH₆ relative to a standard parameter choice.
sections.claimed_result: At the random-phase-approximation level, the authors obtain μ*ME ≈ 0.39 for Mg₂IrH₆ and argue that accounting for energy-dependent density of states resolves a factor-of-two discrepancy between prior Tc estimates.
sections.evidence_type: Computational/theoretical; first-principles screened Coulomb calculations using the Mantel code.
sections.unique_caveat: These are model-based calculations; the inferred Tc shift depends on the screening approximation and material-specific electronic structure, and is not a new superconductivity measurement.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The calculations challenge a widely used input approximation in hydride Tc predictions, quantify a large example effect, and span multiple candidate materials and pressures.

sections.title: A Burst of Reionization in the Dark Ages
sections.abstract: A joint analysis of cosmological data finds a roughly 2–2.5σ preference for an early, temporary reionization contribution from small-scale primordial structure, and forecasts sensitivity for LiteBIRD and the Simons Observatory.
sections.claimed_result: The inferred burst contribution is Δτ ≈ 0.012, with a reported 95% interval of 0.001–0.022; different high-ℓ reprocessings favor different redshift eras, approximately z ≈ 45–165.
sections.evidence_type: Observational-data analysis and forecast; cosmological data including Planck reprocessings, with future mission sensitivity projections.
sections.unique_caveat: The preference is only about 2–2.5σ and the inferred epoch varies materially with the high-ℓ data processing; it is not evidence of a confirmed new reionization episode.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors compare two Planck data reprocessings and report a similar preferred optical-depth contribution; the result connects early structure formation with upcoming CMB polarization tests. The modest significance keeps it below a detection claim.

sections.title: Spinodal-controlled freeze-out and nucleation at the first-order superfluid-supersolid transition of a dipolar gas
sections.abstract: Extended Gross–Pitaevskii simulations of dipolar ¹⁶⁴Dy predict delayed conversion across a first-order superfluid–supersolid transition, dynamical hysteresis and noise-dependent nucleation.
sections.claimed_result: For onsets during linear ramps, the simulated delay from the spinodal has exponent ζ = 0.36 ± 0.02; reverse ramps show a comparable delay, while thermal noise can trigger nucleation before the spinodal.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; three-dimensional extended Gross–Pitaevskii equation with truncated-Wigner noise.
sections.unique_caveat: Without a heat bath, effective nucleation rates depend on preparation; the authors explicitly treat a crossover time inferred from holds as an estimate, not a measured boundary for the ramp protocol.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work supplies a quantitative fitted delay exponent, explores forward and reverse ramps plus thermal-noise scenarios, and is cross-listed in quantum gases and statistical mechanics.
